stem: The sum of the cubes of the consecutive integers from 11 to n inclusive is 8000, that is 11^3 + 12^3 + ... + n^3 = 8000. Using this, find the sum of the squares of the same integers, 11^2 + 12^2 + ... + n^2.

per_option_rationale.rationale: Finds n = 14 correctly but reports the sum of squares of ALL integers 1..14, 14*15*29/6 = 1015, forgetting to subtract the squares of 1..10. The range starts at 11, not 1.
Solves n(n+1)/2 = 105 but reads n = 13 instead of 14 (off by one on the triangular number), then computes 13*14*27/6 - 385 = 819 - 385 = 434. The correct root of n(n+1) = 210 is n = 14.

Uses the right n = 14 and the right range but applies the square-sum formula without the divisor 6, computing (14*15*29) - (10*11*21) = 6090 - 2310 = 3780. The sum-of-squares formula is n(n+1)(2n+1)/6.

explanation_sections.punchline: A range sum is a difference of two prefix sums. Recover n from the cube identity by completing the 1..10 block, then apply the square identity twice and subtract.
explanation_sections.approach: For a series sum over a shifted range, convert to (sum to n) - (sum to start-1) using the closed forms. Back-calculate the unknown index from the given total before computing the target series.
explanation_sections.lesson: Sum of cubes is (n(n+1)/2)^2 and sum of squares is n(n+1)(2n+1)/6; a range that does not start at 1 needs the lower block subtracted.
explanation_sections.timing: About 175 seconds. Fastest elimination is to reject 1015, the all-of-1..14 square sum that forgets the range starts at 11.
